data.title: EU temporarily halts probe into Austrian furniture retailer XXXLutz's German deal
data.description:
The European Commission has temporarily halted its investigation into Austrian furniture retailer XXXLutz's proposed acquisition of German peer Porta to ensure it has received all the information necessary for its review.

  • On November 18, the Commission stopped the clock in its investigation into the acquisition of Porta by XXXLutz, with effect from November 16, a Commission spokesperson said

  • A merger investigation can be suspended if parties fail to provide an important piece of information the Commission has requested for its competition assessment within a prescribed deadline, she added

  • Once the missing information is supplied, the investigation is restarted and the legal deadline for the Commission’s decision is then adjusted accordingly

  • On October 12, EU antitrust investigators opened a full-scale investigation into the merger plan, saying the deal may significantly impact competition in several EU countries, a move which could require XXXLutz to offer remedies to address their concerns

  • The EU set a February 25 deadline for its decision

  • XXXLutz Group said on Thursday it was cooperating "fully and constructively" with the European Commission

  • "In a Phase II investigation, specific issues are examined and assessed in greater detail. This is also the case here," it said

data.title: Time for EMEA investors to stay at home say UBS
data.description:
Key points:
  • STOXX 600 up 0.2%
  • Tech leads gains
  • Anthropic debuts on Nasdaq
  • Nasdaq futures rise 1.7%

TIME FOR EMEA INVESTORS TO STAY AT HOME SAY UBS

After having recently concentrated on a small number of AI-related companies in the US and Asia, investors in EMEA should turn to opportunities closer to home, UBS says, declaring the euro zone its preferred equity region.

"We expect earnings to grow by 15% in 2027, matching our US forecast but from a lower starting valuation and with less dependence on a small group of AI-linked companies," UBS Global Wealth Management's Chief Investment Office writes in a Thursday note.

According to them, investments in defence, infrastructure, automation, power networks, and electrification should support European industrials, while health care can provide a less cyclical earnings stream.

Even as cracks have appeared in the AI trade and its main names have retreated from all-time peaks, the bank believes the industry will continue to be an important earnings driver in 2027.

Still, elevated expectations, questions over monetization, and the concentration of AI exposure in major equity indices all mean investors should look to participate in Europe's broadening earnings and diversify through global commodities, EM bonds and currencies, UBS says.

(Javi West Larrañaga)

data.title: Indonesia defends a sinking rupiah as China reins in a rising yuan - IntelliNews Lambda
data.description:
Bank Indonesia raised rates for the fourth time since May on November 18 to shore up a record-low rupiah, as Beijing works to slow a rising yuan.

A dollar buoyed by bets on another Federal Reserve rise in December is dragging most Asian currencies lower and pushing central banks from Jakarta to Tokyo towards tighter money. China, flush with export earnings, has the opposite trouble: a currency gaining too fast.

Jakarta pays up

Bank Indonesia lifted the BI-Rate by a quarter point to 6.00%, its board said, taking the increase since May to 125 basis points. The rupiah had hit an all-time low of 18,285 per dollar the day before, leaving it about 8.7% weaker this year and the worst performer in emerging Asia, according to Reuters. The bank promised more intervention in offshore non-deliverable forwards and in the onshore spot and forward markets. 'Bank Indonesia remains firmly committed to maintaining Rupiah exchange rate stability by continuing to optimise the full spectrum of monetary instruments,' it said.

Politics made the job harder. The currency's latest leg down followed Vice President Gibran Rakabuming Raka's resignation on November 12, and it had already lost more than 10% against both the Singapore dollar and the ringgit over a year. A central bank that Capital Economics had singled out as the biggest threat to central bank independence among emerging markets now has something to prove, and a surprise rise is one way to prove it.

Policy rates, %, January 2025 to November 19, 2026. China: one-year loan prime rate. Source: BIS, Bank Indonesia, Reserve Bank of India via IntelliNews Lambda

A regional squeeze

Indonesia is the sharpest case, not the only one. The dollar index climbed to 103.81 on November 18, its highest since early April 2025, and futures priced a quarter-point Fed rise next month as close to certain, Investing.com reported. The Philippine peso, down about 8% this year, sits just behind the rupiah, and its bond market is the region's most exposed to Fed tightening.

Japan is tightening for its own reasons, with the yen near 160 per dollar adding to them. Governor Kazuo Ueda told an upper house committee on November 18 that the Bank of Japan would keep raising its policy rate in step with the economy, prices and financial conditions, which he described as still accommodative. A Reuters poll taken on November 11-18 found 61 of 71 economists, or 86%, expecting a rise from 1.25% to 1.50% at the December 17-18 meeting.

In India the pressure shows up in prices. Consumer inflation reached 6.09% in October, up from 5.54% in September, with food prices 8.94% higher, the statistics ministry reported. That breaks the 6% ceiling of the Reserve Bank's 2-6% tolerance band for the first time since the 2024-based index replaced the old series. The central bank had already raised its repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50% on October 7 and moved to what it calls calibrated tightening. With inflation above the policy rate, New Delhi's real rate has slipped below zero.

Policy rate on November 19, 2026 against the latest consumer price inflation, %. Source: Bank Indonesia, Reserve Bank of India, MoSPI, BIS, IMF via IntelliNews Lambda

Beijing leans the other way

China's worry is a currency that is too strong. The yuan gained about 5% against the dollar between the end of 2025 and the end of October, BIS data show, carried by large trade surpluses and exporters converting their dollar receipts. On November 3 the People's Bank of China announced that banks' reserve requirement on foreign currency deposits would rise from 4% to 6% from November 15, the first increase since 2021 and a reversal of the September 2023 cut made when the yuan was sliding.

The central bank framed the step as improving the management of foreign currency liquidity. By Reuters arithmetic it locks up about $24bn of dollars. 'By absorbing part of the available US dollar liquidity in the banking system, it is attempting to reduce the momentum behind yuan appreciation and prevent the market from developing excessive one-way expectations,' Marco Sun, chief financial markets analyst at MUFG Bank (China), told the news agency.

Value against the US dollar, end of month, end-2025 = 100. Source: BIS via IntelliNews Lambda

Same goal, opposite tools

Jakarta is using the price of money, paying savers more to hold rupiah at a cost to borrowers in an economy the government wants to run faster. Beijing is using quantity, draining dollars from its banks while leaving its 3.00% loan prime rate, unchanged since May 2025, alone. Neither is fighting the market head-on. Both want the move slowed, not reversed.

With inflation at 3.23%, Indonesia's 6.00% policy rate leaves a real cushion of nearly 2.8 percentage points. China's inflation of 0.7% gives Beijing room to ease at home even as it reins in its currency. India and Japan, where prices are rising faster than their policy rates, have the least room of all.

December will test all four: the Fed, the Bank of Japan, the Reserve Bank of India and Bank Indonesia all meet before the year is out.

This article was produced with the help of the IntelliNews Lambda analytical tool

data.title: Meta Agrees to Hold Off on Issuing New Stock Until Court Decision
data.description:
By Meghan Bobrowsky

Meta Platforms said it would wait to issue any shares of its new non-voting Class C stock until after a related court case plays out in Delaware this spring.

The company is facing a series of lawsuits brought by shareholders alleging Meta breached its fiduciary duty by approving a deal that investors deemed unfair.

The new class of stock, which has no voting power, is intended to fund Meta's AI bills at a time when the company is on the hook for $825 billion in future spending commitments. In a legal filing, Meta confirmed it would wait until the courtroom process plays out to make any moves.

The company previously said it planned to use the stock to establish an at-the-market stock offering program of up to $60 billion, potentially beginning in the first quarter of 2027. The new shares also gave Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg a way to sell equity to potentially pay a California wealth tax without losing any voting power.

In a statement, a Meta spokesman said the company is "seeking a final determination as quickly as the court will allow," and that it would "vigorously defend" itself against the claims in the lawsuits.

Write to Meghan Bobrowsky at meghan.bobrowsky@wsj.com

data.title: Babcock Shares Climb on Earnings Beat, Push Into Drones
data.description:
By Michael Hennessey

Babcock International Group shares jumped after the defense group reported higher-than-expected earnings and set out new growth plans focused on autonomous drones and national infrastructure security.

Shares climbed 8.15% to 10.55 pounds on Thursday morning and led the FTSE 100 index, which was trading 0.2% lower.

The defense group said revenue in the six months to the end of September rose 6.3% to 2.70 billion pounds ($3.55 billion), ahead of a consensus estimate provided by Visible Alpha of 2.64 billion pounds.

Operating profit--Babcock's preferred profitability metric--fell to 220.7 million pounds from 234.3 million pounds against tough prior-year comparisons boosted by one-off accounting gains. Operating profit was ahead of analysts' expectations of 215.0 million pounds. Operating costs grew to 2.48 billion pounds from 2.30 billion pounds.

Underlying operating profit climbed to 227.3 million pounds from 201.1 million pounds, helped by a strong performance in nuclear and aviation.

Looking ahead, the company outlined new initiatives to improve its performance under its new chief executive, Harry Holt, who succeeded David Lockwood earlier this year.

Babcock will seek additional growth by focusing on the "new nature of warfare," the company said. It will invest more in mixed human and drone technology that will connect modern unmanned equipment with traditional crewed systems.

The company will also push into national strategic resilience, including by upgrading critical national infrastructure and helping the U.K. obtain greater energy security.

As part of this strategy, Babcock said it is currently tracking opportunities to provide counter-drone protection for civil and military national infrastructure in France, Canada and the Middle East.

"As customer requirements evolve, we are increasingly focused on delivering connected, technology-enabled and adaptable solutions that help allied forces maintain operational advantage," Holt said.

Babcock's new growth vectors are viewed as an additive to a core business that should continue to benefit from multiyear contract opportunities, analysts at Jefferies wrote in a note to clients.

The company reaffirmed its outlook for the year ending in March, as well as its medium-term expectations. It said around 90% of revenue for the year was under contract at the start of October.

The London-listed company declared an interim dividend of 2.8 pence per share, up from 2.5 pence a year ago.

Write to Michael Hennessey at michael.hennessey@wsj.com

data.title: Anthropic IPO Lifts Mood in Markets — WSJ
data.description:
By Rebecca Feng

Futures tied to the tech-heavy Nasdaq index jumped more than 2% on expectations of a pop in Anthropic trading, after the Claude maker pulled off a record-breaking initial public offering.

Futures tied to the S&P 500 also jumped more than 1%, pointing to a day of gains after five consecutive down days.

Ahead of their public debut on the Nasdaq today, Anthropic's shares are trading as much as 25% above their IPO price of $83 a share in the grey market. That price was set above the company's target range of $70 to $78 a share.

Investors view Anthropic's IPO as a major test for the artificial intelligence trade. Strong demand for the AI giant's shares helped ease recent fears surrounding the AI bubble and temporarily diverted investors' attention away from the dramatic departure of Jensen Huang from Nvidia.

Frank Downing, director of research at ARK Investment Management, which has been an investor in Anthropic since 2023, said on CNBC today that the company's IPO is a huge milestone, but still "very early" in what will be a spectacular run for these software and AI companies.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
